title: Amazing Grace
description: The best-loved English-language hymn, sung to the pentatonic folk tune "New Britain". Its slow 3/4 sway and one-note-per-syllable melody make it an ideal first piece for lyrical, singing legato.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: Single-note melody in an extended G position with the left hand holding one root-fifth dyad per bar.
teachingPoints: RH stays in G position (thumb on G4) and reaches down to D4/E4 with the thumb for the low notes
The tune starts on a pickup D4: count 1-2 before you play, then land G4 on the downbeat
Practise the B4-G4 eighth-note pairs (bars 2, 6, 10, 14) slowly so they do not rush
Hold every LH dyad for the full three beats; keep the fifth light under the melody

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: Adds harmony notes under the melody (thirds and sixths) and a root-then-chord waltz bass with E minor and D7 colour chords.
teachingPoints: LH pattern is root on beat 1, two-note chord on beats 2-3: practise the hand alone until the leap is automatic
Watch the walking bass D3 at the end of bars 5, 7, 11 and 13 that pulls the harmony back to G
RH dyads in bars 7-9 (D5 over F#4) need a relaxed hand; keep the melody note on top louder
Final cadence: balance the three-note RH chord so G4 still sings above the fifth in the bass
